headline: 164 dead as twin earthquakes strike Venezuela, 1,000 injured
summary: Twin quakes measuring 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude hit west of Caracas, leaving dozens of buildings in rubble and thousands feared missing.
details: Twin earthquakes measuring 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude struck west of Caracas, Venezuela, leaving at least 164 people dead and nearly 1,000 injured.
The northern region of La Guaira was the hardest hit and has been declared a disaster zone. Caracas's international airport, located in this region, has been closed.
In Catia La Mar, widespread destruction was reported across nearly 200 housing towers. Many buildings were reduced to rubble, while others suffered deep structural cracks.
Survivors describe scenes of devastation, with many residents spending the night in the streets due to power outages and fear of aftershocks.
Emergency teams are struggling with limited resources. Jose Pacheco, chief of the United Rescue Group of Venezuela, stated he has never seen destruction on this scale in 30 years.
Rescuers continue to pull bodies from the debris as reports of people trapped under the rubble continue to flood in.
caption:
164 dead and nearly 1,000 injured after twin 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude earthquakes devastate Venezuela.

Twin earthquakes measuring 7.2 and 7.5 magnitude struck west of Caracas, Venezuela, leaving at least 164 people dead and nearly 1,000 injured.

The northern region of La Guaira was the hardest hit and has been declared a disaster zone. Caracas's international airport, located in this region, has been closed.

In Catia La Mar, widespread destruction was reported across nearly 200 housing towers. Many buildings were reduced to rubble, while others suffered deep structural cracks.

Survivors describe scenes of devastation, with many residents spending the night in the streets due to power outages and fear of aftershocks.

Emergency teams are struggling with limited resources. Jose Pacheco, chief of the United Rescue Group of Venezuela, stated he has never seen destruction on this scale in 30 years.

Rescuers continue to pull bodies from the debris as reports of people trapped under the rubble continue to flood in.

headline: Bangladesh Bank removes lending cap on consumer loans to boost spending
summary: The banking regulator has lifted the annual limit on the amount banks can lend to individuals, aiming to stimulate consumer spending.
details: Bangladesh Bank has lifted the annual limit on the amount of loans banks can extend to individuals to boost consumer spending.
The banking regulator announced the decision on Thursday, stating that banks will now have no limits on the total amount they can lend to the consumer sector.
This limit had been in place since 2017, which mandated that the growth rate of consumer loans could not exceed the growth rate of a bank's total loans.
Despite the removal of the overall sector limit, the loan limits for individual borrowers remain unchanged.
The tenure of consumer loans will not exceed eight years, although longer tenures are permitted for housing and home construction sectors.
To further encourage the purchase of electric vehicles, Bangladesh Bank previously increased the individual loan limit for electric and hybrid vehicles to Tk 8 million on May 5.
The loan-investment ratio for electric and hybrid vehicle loans has also been improved to 80:20 percent, up from the previous 60:40 percent.
caption:
No more limits on consumer loans! Bangladesh Bank is moving to boost spending across the country.

Bangladesh Bank has lifted the annual limit on the amount of loans banks can extend to individuals to boost consumer spending.

The banking regulator announced the decision on Thursday, stating that banks will now have no limits on the total amount they can lend to the consumer sector.

This limit had been in place since 2017, which mandated that the growth rate of consumer loans could not exceed the growth rate of a bank's total loans.

Despite the removal of the overall sector limit, the loan limits for individual borrowers remain unchanged.

The tenure of consumer loans will not exceed eight years, although longer tenures are permitted for housing and home construction sectors.

To further encourage the purchase of electric vehicles, Bangladesh Bank previously increased the individual loan limit for electric and hybrid vehicles to Tk 8 million on May 5.

The loan-investment ratio for electric and hybrid vehicle loans has also been improved to 80:20 percent, up from the previous 60:40 percent.
